method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of Rice's theorem, index-set characterization, diagonal proof and corollary, with exact formula, macro, label and reference parity. The QA parser was extended for nested dollar math in text macros; its results on all 244 prior units were unchanged. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Decidability of extensional properties of partial computable functions, program syntax versus behavior, s-m-n reduction from K and four undecidable index-set examples.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The Tot proof did not rely on a special totality feature: for x in K its h could act like any chosen partial computable function. The standard φ_0,φ_1,... enumeration supports Rice's theorem: if the index set A={n:φ_n∈C} is computable for a class C of partial computable functions, C is empty or contains them all.
samples.checks: The Tot reference, constant-zero example, partial-function universe, A/C roles and empty-versus-all conclusion are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An index set contains either all or none of the indices computing each fixed function. Therefore Rice's theorem says no nontrivial such set is decidable. Syntactic questions about a program's symbols, lines, while statement or literal hello world in a print call can be decidable; behavioral questions about halting on zero, ever halting or producing an even number cannot be nontrivially decidable.
samples.checks: The extensional invariance, syntax-behavior distinction, literal code examples, numeric thresholds and three behavior examples are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Assume C is nonempty and proper, and choose the nowhere-defined f outside C and some g inside C, switching C with its complement if needed. Define h(x,y) to be undefined when φ_x(x) diverges and otherwise to behave as g(y). Operationally simulate φ_x(x), then g(y); formally strict composition with projection of g(y) and Un(x,x) requires both computations to be defined.
samples.checks: The without-loss switch, two C-membership roles, divergence case, sequence of simulations and both-argument strictness of the projection formula are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For fixed x, h_x equals f if φ_x(x) is undefined and equals g otherwise. Since h is partial computable, s-m-n yields primitive-recursive s(e,x) indexing h_x. Thus x∈K iff s(e,x)∈A; a computable A would make K computable, contradiction.
samples.checks: The case distinction, index e, primitive-recursive s, defined versus up-arrow notation and K-to-A reduction direction are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The corollary lists undecidable index sets: programs whose range contains 17, whose partial function is constant, whose function is total, and whose outputs satisfy the source's universally stated increasing-value condition. Each class is extensional and neither empty nor all functions.
samples.checks: All four protected formulas, inner text-math tokens and nontrivial-index-set justification are preserved.

source_observations: T334 records निर्देशांकसंच and अतुच्छ गुणधर्म as source-defined specialist compounds; the theorem's extensional restriction comes from OpenLogic rather than a lexical source.

The QA math extractor now pairs outer dollars at brace depth zero, preserving nested text-math tokens in the corollary. Regression against the last public parser produced identical checks for all 244 previously recorded units.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The index-set and nontrivial-property compounds remain expert-reviewable.
The source's fourth corollary predicate is translated as written; this checkpoint does not simplify its quantified condition.
